== Course of events ==

The declaration follows directly upon the Witch's death: Dorothy, having thrown water over her captor in anger, watched the Witch melt away, bringing her tyranny over the Winkies to an end. In the immediate aftermath, with the Witch's rule shattered and no one left to enforce it, Dorothy declares the Winkies free from slavery, ending years of cruel servitude under the Witch.

The declaration comes at a moment when the Witch's household and the wider Winkie people had long lived under her command, a servitude the surrounding events only gesture toward through the presence of Winkies still carrying out tasks for their former captors. With the Witch gone and Dorothy the one who caused her death, it falls to Dorothy to pronounce the Winkies' liberation, formally closing the period of their bondage.

The freeing of the Winkies stands as the clearest resolution of the Witch's downfall, converting Dorothy's act of self-defense into a lasting change for the people who had suffered under the Witch. It is in the space opened by this declaration that Dorothy turns her attention to her captured companions, beginning with freeing the Cowardly Lion once she learns of the Witch's end.
